answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a zenith as the anchor of the cost.
